disclaimer: Reminder reference only — NOT legal authority. Seasons are subject to change after the booklets were printed (notably wolf trapping, which is the subject of a federal lawsuit). Always verify current seasons, emergency changes, unit boundaries, and the federal-court closure map with IDFG before trapping.

license_summary.trapping_license: An Idaho trapping license is required. Mandatory furtaker report due to Fish and Game by July 31 each year (online via GoOutdoorsIdaho.com or paper); failure to report blocks next year's license.
license_summary.mandatory_check: Bobcat and river otter: mandatory check, report, and pelt tags. Raw bobcat pelts need an official export tag; raw otter pelts need an official state export tag within 72 hours after the close of season.
license_summary.controlled_beaver: Controlled Beaver Trapping Units 201, 202, 203 require a valid unit permit; applications due Sep 15; contact the listed person by Oct 14; mandatory controlled beaver report within 10 days of the season close.
license_summary.wolf: Wolf trapping requires a trapping license with Wolf Trapper Education course validation plus wolf tag(s).

permit_requirements: Idaho trapping license with Wolf Trapper Education course validation
species.notes: Wolves are managed under Idaho's big game rules and have separate hunting and trapping seasons — this entry models TRAPPING only. A valid trapping license WITH Wolf Trapper Education course validation and wolf tag(s) is required. Wolf tags are valid for the calendar year. Any person wishing to trap wolves must first complete the Idaho wolf trapper education/certification course. Diverters are optional but encouraged in moose country; minimum loop stops and breakaway devices are recommended. Idaho wolf trapping seasons are the subject of a lawsuit in federal court. Before placing wolf traps, trappers are responsible for checking the IDFG website to confirm what seasons are open: idfg.idaho.gov/rules/big-game. Wolf trapping seasons in 19 Idaho counties are closed due to the federal court decision (see booklet page 83 map).

verification.confirmation_notes: Both booklets are the 2026-27 editions (upland booklet covers '2026 & 2027 Seasons & Rules'; big game covers July 2026–June 2027). Regional furbearer tables are printed identically across regions except fox (Panhandle/Clearwater Oct 10–Mar 31; all other regions year-round). Otter quotas and per-trapper limit read from booklet page 33. Wolf trapping tables were verified against rendered PDF page images (booklet pp. 81-83) because text extraction garbled the unit/season/method columns.
known_gaps: Wolf trapping: the season dates in the booklet are the subject of a federal lawsuit; the app must direct users to idfg.idaho.gov/rules/big-game before placing traps. The 19-county federal-court closure map (booklet p. 83) is not encoded as polygons — zones are descriptive.
Beaver/otter closed drainages and WMAs (regional exceptions) are summarized, not enumerated.
Scientific names are standard taxonomy, NOT stated in the IDFG booklets — all flagged scientific_name_verified=false.
Panhandle and Clearwater regions observe Pacific Time; Mountain Time is used elsewhere.
Detailed method rules (beaver house/den protection, otter trap-size rule when mink/marten closed, bait-distance rules, IDFG Access Program restrictions) are noted, not fully modeled.
